 Starting XI: Will Le Bris Make These Seven Changes For Sunderland’s Game In Poznan?
 Who would you pick today? Let us know in the comments below.
 by Martin Wanless Oct 22, 2026, 5:00 AM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 LEIRIA, PORTUGAL - OCTOBER 15: The shirts of Trai Hume, Malick Fofana and Timur Tutierov are displayed inside the Sunderland dressing room before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Octavio Passos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) UEFA via Getty Images Well, after that debacle on Sunday we have an opportunity to get into some form ahead of a big game at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Unfortunately it’s impossible to look at this team selection in isolation as Sunday’s got to come into the manager’s thinking – so here’s the team I think he’ll go with this afternoon.
 Goalkeeper: Robin Roefs
 A bright spark on an awful afternoon last weekend, Roefs will be hoping for another solid game tonight as he regains his form.
 BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Sunderland’s Robin Roefs during the Premier League 2026/27 match between AFC Bournemouth and Sunderland at Vitality Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Bournemouth, United Kingdom. (Photo by David Horton - CameraSport via Getty Images) CameraSport via Getty Images Defence: Trai Hume, Kevin Danso, Luke O’Nien, Dayann Methalie
 Danso barely had time to stretch his legs on Sunday, and given our injury concerns at the back and he’s not available for Sunday, I think Le Bris has to play the big Austrian defender today – probably alongside Luke O’Nien. We know Alderete is far better than what he’s shown recently, but given he’s only just come back from injury asking him to play a third game in a week is likely too much. At full back, we’ll probably see Hume and Methalie – it’s a big opportunity for the latter to play his way into the team. After an impressive display at the Etihad he was disappointing last Thursday, so hopefully we’ll see more of his marauding runs forward as I think he could be a valuable attacking weapon down the flank.
 LEIRIA, PORTUGAL - OCTOBER 15: Manu Pozo of SC Uniao Torreense is challenged by Dayann Methalie of Sunderland during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estádio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Octavio Passos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) UEFA via Getty Images Midfield: Jules Ahoka, Enzo Le Fee, Habib Diarra
 It’s a difficult one with Xhaka. Is he knackered, or just out of form? If it’s the former he needs a rest, the latter he needs to play. I think he’ll be on the bench again today, but personally I’d play him. Jules Ahoka is a cert, having played so well last Thursday, and there’s a real chance a good showing today will get him a starting place against Leeds. Le Fee was on the bench last Thursday so could come into the starting line up today as Rigg was poor on Sunday and Sadiki’s minutes need managing (I don’t think he’s looked anywhere near his best yet this season, either). One player who could get a chance is Habib Diarra – I reckon he will get an hour from the start as he looks to build back to fitness. Again, a good display from him will have him in contention for Sunday.
 BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 18: Sunderland’s Habib Diarra during the Premier League 2026/27 match between AFC Bournemouth and Sunderland at Vitality Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Bournemouth, United Kingdom. (Photo by David Horton - CameraSport via Getty Images) CameraSport via Getty Images Striker: Nilson Angulo, Trey Ogunsuyi, Malick Fofana
 Angulo and Fofana need games to get them into some sort of form, and both will likely start on the wings. The big question is who plays through the middle? Brobbey and Isidor won’t make it, so the options are Tutierov or Trey Ogunsuyi, or play a midfielder out of position. I think we might give Ogunsuyi a chance. Is it ideal? Probably not, but he’s 19 and if he’s going to have a future with us he needs to prove himself sooner rather than later. He’s a more natural striker than Tutierov, was on the bench on Sunday, so could well get a start.
 YORK, ENGLAND - JULY 18: Trey Samuel-Ogunsuyi of Sunderland runs with the ball during the Pre-season friendly match between York City and Sunderland at LNER Community Stadium on July 18, 2026 in York, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images) Getty Images See More : MATCH PREVIEWS!
